Raw materials :For the nine-month  period  of 2025  (9M2025 ), the ratio  of raw material  
costs  to total  revenue  slightly  decreased  from  37.7% to 37.5%, mainly  due to lower  
prices  of key raw materials  such as synthetic  rubber  and silicone . Most  of the 
Company’s  automotive  segment  revenue  relies  on synthetic  rubber,  the price  of which  
dropped  by approximately  4–5% compared  with the previous  year,  resulting  in a 
lower  overall  raw material  cost ratio .
The downward  trend  in raw material  prices  has continued,  according  to the 
raw material  price  index  for 2024–2025 , particularly  for synthetic  rubber,  whose  price  
has steadily  declined  since  the fourth  quarter  of 2024 , when  it reached  its peak .Depreciation and Amortization :
Depreciation and amortization expenses slightly declined in absolute terms. With a significant 
increase in revenue, the proportion of these fixed costs to revenue dropped from 9.6% to 7.5%, 
indicating more efficient utilization of production capacity.
Other overhead cost : 
Other manufacturing costs increased by THB 20.8 million, mainly due to higher spending on 
factory consumables and maintenance of buildings and machinery, in line with revenue growth. 
The ratio of other manufacturing costs to total revenue rose by 0.4% compared with the same 
period last year. This was primarily due to new consumer product lines that required a higher 
proportion of consumable materials, together with initial testing and process optimization costs, 
which temporarily elevated the cost ratio during the period.Labor cost :For the nine-month  period  of 2025 , labor  costs  increased  by THB 18.0 million  YoY, 
primarily  from  higher  production  volumes  in both  the automotive  and consumer  product  
segments . However,  labor  costs  as a percentage  of revenue  declined  by 0.5%, from  the previous  
year to 12.8%, due to the Company’s  effective  control  of overtime  expenses,  improved  
production  planning,  and the adoption  of automation  systems  to streamline  operations  and 
enhance  efficiency . Another  supporting  factor  was the higher  utilization  rate,  which  allowed  
fixed  labor  costs  such as those  related  to production  support,  warehouse  management,  and 
indirect  labor—to be spread  across  a larger  output  base,  thereby  lowering  the cost per unit.

Business outlook : Automotive
Opportunities
•Expansion  of production  capacity  for new, highly  complex  projects . This is a 
key driver  behind  the segment’s  Gross  Margin  improvement  from 
20.5% → 26.4% this year.
•Investment  in robots  and automation  systems  to enhance  high-precision  
manufacturing  capability,  strengthen  cost competitiveness,  and support  
upcoming  mass production  volumes .Support factors
•Domestic  automotive  production  began  to recover  in Q3/2025.
•Prices  of synthetic  rubber  and silicone  continue  to trend downward  in 2025.The automotive  business  remains  the company’s  core growth  driver,  supported  
by several  new projects  currently  “in hand”  and progressing  toward  mass 
production . However,  the timeline  may shift to Q1 next year due to the impact  
of recent  U.S. import  tariff policies . Overall  momentum  remains  positive,  
supported  by key factors :

## Page 19

Business outlook : Consumer products
Support factors
•Despite  Thailand’s  modest  economic  growth,  this product  group  is distributed  
across  multiple  countries . Strong  demand  from international  markets  
mitigates  domestic  economic  slowdown  risks.
•Throughout  2025, raw materials  such as plastic  resins  and silicone  have 
shown  a continued  downward  price trend,  enabling  the division  to maintain  
healthy  profitability
Progress & Strategic Direction
•New products  from global  brand  customers  will commence  mass production  in 
Q4, driving  strong  year-end revenue .
•Additional  newly  developed  items will also begin  revenue  recognition  in Q4.
•Continuous  investment  in production  automation  to Improve  consistency  in 
product  quality  and reduce  labor costs.The Consumer  Products  division  is entering  a renewed  growth  phase  toward  the 
end of this year, with several  new products  scheduled  to begin  mass production  
in Q4, from both existing  and new clients—particularly  global  brand  customers,  
which  remain  a key strength  of the company .

## Page 20

Business outlook : Medical devices
•Medical -grade  packaging  for pharmaceuticals  and infusion  solutions  made  
from high-performance  specialty  plastics . Testing  has been completed,  and 
mass production  is targeted  for Q2 next year.
•Continued  expansion  into silicone -based  and specialty -plastic  medical  
components,  leveraging  core expertise  to maintain  competitiveness  and 
high margin  levels .Opportunities
Support factors
•Global  demand  for medical  products  remains  strong,  particularly  for single -use 
and disposable  components —key structural  trends  in the post-COVID  era.
•This division  continues  to deliver  the company’s  highest  profitability,  with 
Medical  Gross  Margin  at 65%, maintained  even during  the mid-year volume  
slowdownDespite  trade-policy  challenges  earlier  this year, the Medical  division  is now firmly  
in recovery . With new high-margin  products  entering  production  and additional  
projects  commencing  next year, continued  growth  is expected .
